chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazal, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazeed (and he is Farqad), from Abi Yazeed al-Hammarr, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah the Exalted sent four angels for the destruction of the people of Lut: Jibra'il, Mikail, Israfil, and Karoubil (peace be upon them). They passed by Ibrahim (peace be upon him) while they were veiled (with turbans). They greeted him, but he did not recognize them. He saw their good appearance and said, 'No one will serve these except myself personally.' He was a host of guests, so he grilled a fat calf for them until it was cooked, then brought it near to them. When he placed it before them, he saw their hands not reaching for it, so he noted it and felt fear from them.

When Jibra'il (peace be upon him) saw that, he removed the turban from his face and head. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) recognized him and said, 'You are he.' He said, 'Yes.' His wife Sarah passed by, and he gave her the good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq of Yaqub. She said, 'What did Allah the Mighty and Majestic say?' They answered her with what is in the Mighty Book.
Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to them, 'For what have you come?' They said to him, 'For the destruction of the people of Lut.'

He said to them, 'If there were a hundred believers among them, would you destroy them?' Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said, 'No.' He said, 'If there were fifty?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'If there were thirty?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'If there were twenty?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'If there were ten?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'If there were five?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'If there was one?' He said, 'No.'
He said, 'Surely in it is Lut.' They said, 'We know well who is in it; we shall certainly deliver him and his family, except his wife; she shall be of those who remain behind.'

Then they left. And Al-Hasan al-Askari (Abu Muhammad) said, 'I do not know this statement except that it preserves them, and it is the Statement of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: 'He began to plead with Us for Lut's people.' So they came to Lut while he was in his farm near the city. They greeted him while they were veiled.

When he saw them, he saw a good appearance; they had white turbans and white robes. He said to them, 'Lodging?' They said, 'Yes.' He led them and they walked behind him. He regretted having offered them lodging and said, 'What shall I do when I come to my people with them, and I know them?'

So he turned to them and said, 'You have come to the evil creatures of Allah.' And Jibra'il (peace be upon him) had said, 'We will not make haste against them until he testifies with three testimonies.'

Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said, 'This is one testimony.' Then they walked for a while, then he turned to them and said, 'You have come to the evil creatures of Allah.' Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said, 'These are two testimonies.' Then they went, and when they reached the gate of the city, he turned to them and said, 'You have come to the evil creatures of Allah.' Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said, 'This is the third testimony.'

Then he entered and they entered with him. When his wife saw them, she saw a good appearance, so she climbed onto the roof and whistled. When they did not hear her, she raised smoke. When they saw the smoke, they came rushing to the door. She came down to them and said, 'He has people with him whom I have never seen with better appearance than theirs.'
They came to the door to enter. When Lut saw them, he stood up to them and said, 'O people! Fear Allah and do not disgrace me regarding my guests. Is there no man of guidance among you?'
He said, 'These are my daughters; they are cleaner for you.' So he called them to the Halal. They said, 'You know what is our right in your daughters, and you know what we want.'

He said, 'If I had strength against you or I could resort to a strong support.' Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said, 'If only he knew what strength he has.' So they spoke much to him until they entered the house.

Jibra'il (peace be upon him) shouted to him, 'O Lut! Let them enter.' When they entered, Jibra'il (peace be upon him) pointed his finger towards them, so their eyesight was lost. And it is His Statement: 'But We blinded their eyes.'

Then Jibra'il called out and said, 'We are the messengers of your Lord; they will not reach you.' So travel with your family by night. And Jibra'il said to him, 'We have been sent for their destruction.'
He said, 'O Jibra'il, hurry up.' He said, 'Their appointed time is the morning. Is not the morning yet?'

So he commanded him to carry and whoever was with him except his wife. Then Jibra'il uprooted her with his wings from the seven earths, then raised her until the inhabitants of the sky of the world heard the barking of the dogs and the crowing of the rooster.
Then he overturned her and rained upon her and upon those around the city stones of clay.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Lut's three testimonies before the destruction of his people in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elaborates on the narrative of the angels' visit to Ibrahim and Lut, highlighting the specific role of Jibra'il in guiding Lut and the theological nuance that the angels did not rush the destruction until Lut had publicly testified three times to his people's corruption. It further details the miraculous elevation of Lut's wife from the seven earths, illustrating the completeness of her exclusion from the saved, while emphasizing the angels' patience and the specific mechanism of divine punishment through the blinding of the people.
